title: ICE cotton rises further on crop concerns, weaker US dollar
content:
ICE cotton futures rose for a second session; December 2026 settled at 85.48 cents, a fresh 3-month high, as volume and open interest strengthened. 
China’s reserve sale recorded its 21st consecutive 100 per cent sold-out auction, while ICE certified stocks fell to 72,626 bales. 
US crop condition fell to 38 per cent Good + Excellent, with hot, dry West Texas weather the main production risk.

title: Bangladesh, India discuss trade barriers during CII visit
content:
A CII delegation led by Chandrajit Banerjee is in Dhaka for talks on trade, investment and industrial co-operation with Bangladesh.
Meetings with ministers and FBCCI matter for apparel, jute and wider manufacturing suppliers facing tariff and non-tariff issues.
Trade data points to a large imbalance, keeping market access and Indian investment in Bangladesh on the agenda.

title: Asian lyocell buying could split as September demand approaches
content:
Regional lyocell markets moved in three directions between August 10 and 14, 2026, with TexPro showing local demand and liquidity driving Asian MMCF pricing.
China domestic 1.4D lyocell firmed to CNY 13,600 per metric tonne, gaining 0.89 per cent over the week.
India held at ₹203 per kilogram, while Pakistan eased to PKR 693 per kilogram after a 0.43 per cent fall.

title: Bangladesh to adopt April-March fiscal year from FY 2028-29
content:
Bangladesh’s cabinet has approved a shift in the fiscal year to April 1-March 31 from FY 2028-29, replacing the current July 1-June 30 cycle.
FY 2027-28 will be a nine-month transition ending in March, placing manufacturers, exporters and importers under a changed budget calendar.
The Cabinet Division said the change is intended to help finish infrastructure work before the monsoon.

title: Autumn orders could decide the next move in China FDY prices
content:
Chinese domestic polyester filament yarn prices firmed selectively, led by fine-denier FDY 150D/96F, up 0.58 per cent week on week to 8.70 CNY/kg on TexPro.
FDY 75D/36F gained 0.28 per cent to 8,975 CNY/mt, while coarser FDY 100D/72F held at 8,750 CNY/mt through the week.
The move was cost-supported rather than demand-led, putting margins, inventory decisions and sourcing plans in focus.

title: India’s growth remains resilient; Q1 GDP seen at 7.3%: Report
content:
CareEdge sees India’s Q1 FY27 GDP growth at 7.3 per cent and lifts its FY27 forecast to 7 per cent. 
Manufacturing growth is seen rising to 9.9 per cent, with factory output, tax collections, auto output and imports signalling stronger activity. 
Supply chains face watchpoints from West Asia energy risks, slower goods trade growth, trade-policy uncertainty and El Nino.

title: How will Cambodia’s 6 strategies boost business competitiveness?
content:
Cambodia’s Ministry of Commerce has outlined six strategies to boost business competitiveness, spanning public-private cooperation, product quality, digital trade, supply chains, foreign investment and new market access. 
For textile, apparel, footwear and travel goods firms, the focus on packaging, standards compliance and logistics efficiency could support export readiness and lower costs.

title: How did Acushnet boost South Korea's Misto Holdings’ Q2 results?
content:
Misto Holdings’ Q2 sales rose 16.6 per cent year on year, with operating profit up 62.3 per cent on Acushnet growth, cost efficiency and a tariff refund. 
Acushnet sales rose 21.7 per cent as golf balls, clubs and gear gained from launches, higher prices and optimised timing. 
Fila’s domestic shoes and clothing improved, overseas stores expanded in Malaysia, and JUUN.J opened stores in China.

title: What is behind Japan's Asics’ record-breaking H1 performance?
content:
Asics posted record Q2 FY26 results, with first-half net sales up 32.7 per cent to ¥534.4 billion (~$3.36 billion and operating profit up 48.5 per cent.
SportStyle, Onitsuka Tiger and Performance Running drove growth, with sales and profit rising across all major regions.
Margin gains, cost control and lower inventories helped offset tariffs and costs; Asics lifted FY26 sales and profit outlook.

title: China+1 is evolving into China+proof for apparel sourcing
content:
TexPro data shows eight Asian hubs gained share equal to 90.8 per cent of China's US apparel share loss between 2021 and 2025.
Cambodia shows the clearest rerouting risk signal, with Chinese textile exports and finished-apparel shipments to Cambodia rising sharply.
Vietnam, Bangladesh and India look more like manufacturing platforms using Chinese inputs as origin proof becomes critical.
